comments.text:
On Larptubers (LTs):

I was made aware of LT through "The Larping Tombstone" (LT The Living Tombstone TLT) who has been making fun memey songs very much in tune with "classic" TLT. 

They have been exploding in subs and views because the content is high quality and the real TLT has been on tour, thus putting out less content. Larpstone actually has had the music stolen and put on Spotify because they don't want to without permission first. 

I personally see this trend as more ethical fan channels (channels of live streamers who condense and edit segments in a way similar to their main channel. All while being monetized. Sometimes being so good that they are almost indistinguishable from uploads, and even being hired by the people they make content of. 

I see LT as a similar practice to hone production, editing, and content styles through mimicry. With nobody actually believing them to be real, but nostalgic for early 2010s YT/ society. 

While the situation of Technolarp certainly is a bit off-putting, especially in the skinwalker with friends collab situation, I don't feel that Technolarp did anything objectively wrong. His videos funded charity, to my knowledge, none of the jokes or comments were done in bad faith. He stopped as soon as he got an affirmative no. 

In a world of defense contractors and rampant gambling scams/ insider trading, I think Moist/Charlie is speaking from a place of immense privilege to chew him out over a secondary donation link. 

If someone is utilizing a massive audience and a YT trend that also raises money for charity, I think homie deserves to also get paid by people who want to support him specifically.

comments.text:
The larptube community isn’t necessarily a cohesive group but rather a collection of people that imitate other often larger and well established creators, typically modeling their videos off of the older styles of videos that the creator no longer makes. The more bootleg the better imo

A good example of the larp community I feel is Larpiplier, who does a good vocal and visual impression of early Markiplier on top of maintaining the original feel of his videos, not only doing lets plays of Amnesia but also newer games in the style of these older videos. The Larping Videogame Nerd is another that adds to the joy of seeing people recreating the styles of these YouTubers just with new subject matters, like getting new episodes of a show you used to watch. Of course anyone can be a larp tuber, it’s just that to keep your audience you have to be good at being a knockoff funnily enough.

There are channels like Technolarp where the line definitely gets drawn, with creators who have passed typically being frowned upon, yet apparently there are enough people in Technoblade’s audience who don’t perceive the moral dilemma of growing the channel of someone larping as technoblade. The person should have originally thought more about how this should have been a one off idea that should not be put into action, but alas that’s not what happened. 

What I hope that people understand is that this community doesn’t necessarily have a way to choose who gets larped, and that a large part of the people making these channels are doing so out of a love for old YouTube, wanting to bring back their favorite moments in a way that honors what this website meant to them. There’s debates to be had sure, but I think that seeing the larptube community overall as regressive and antisocial is harmful, and that hopefully greater understanding can be achieved.
